bodyMarkdown:
## Definition of progressive specification

Progressive specification is the practice of making design decisions increasingly specific as understanding increases. In Creative Navy's lexicon, the movement is research to requirements to specifications to system.

The principle is that early work should not lock detailed system decisions before the terrain is understood. Early phases work at a higher level of abstraction. Later phases resolve detail. Specificity is earned through exploration rather than assumed at the start.

Progressive specification is closely related to organic system building. A system cannot be made specific by imposing a complete structure before the work has revealed what the system needs to be. Progressive specification is the way specificity is built without being imposed prematurely.

## Why progressive specification exists

Progressive specification addresses the failure mode of front-loaded specification. In a front-loaded model, the full system is specified at the start of the engagement based on initial understanding. The risk is that the engagement's own research later contradicts the initial specification.

Progressive specification treats early work as exploratory. Sandbox Experiments explore rather than specify. Later structural work becomes more precise as the engagement produces better understanding.

The same principle appears in the four-iteration architecture pattern described in the source evidence. Iteration 1 establishes broad logic. Iteration 4 resolves detailed optimisation. The structure becomes more specific as understanding becomes more reliable.

## AIT shows specification changing during a design block

AIT evidence records a controller structure specification of roughly 900 nodes across eleven levels of hierarchy, written in German, that changed during the design block. In one revision, a single operating-mode setting became four settings, one for each heating and mixing circuit.

This is a direct example of progressive specification. The work did not assume the final operating-mode structure at the start. The specification became more specific as the design block clarified what the controller structure required.

## The MDU shows specification revision after design reviews

The MDU evidence records a specification that changed because of design reviews, with the before and after versions in hand. The revision issued after the reviews added four draught inputs and an offset derivation, added pitch period where the earlier specification carried roll period only, added ship breadth, added event logging and data logging, and promoted 48-hour data logging from a cost-driven nice-to-have into the main specification.

This example shows progressive specification as a documented movement from understanding to specification. The change log records what the design process produced, rather than presenting the final specification as if it had been fully known at the start.

## Egma shows progressive specification through layered disclosure and ordering flow

Egma and Egma Order show progressive specification in two related interface structures. In one documented revision, eleven production steps were resolved into three layers of disclosure. The client proposed a disclosure model with four headline states, current sub-status on hover and the full breakdown on click. Creative Navy resolved the delivered design into three headline groups: Order Processed, In Production and Delivery, spanning eleven production steps. The Orders area was also split into drafts, in progress and complete.

Egma Order also shows specificity through a sequence for choosing from approximately 7,000 lens types. The flow offered repeat-a-past-order first, because most stores reorder the same few types. It then used filtering by eight criteria: brand, index, sphere, cylinder, sub-technology, coating, sun protection and diameter. It then added a quantities step in which the interface auto-calculates the percentage each lens type represents of the total, allowing the optometrist to judge the distribution on the spot.

The Egma evidence does not report measured platform performance. It shows how a catalogue and a production-state model were made tractable through staged specification.

## KISPE Space shows progressive specification as artefact-chain change control

KISPE Space, a UK space systems engineering company, shows progressive specification as a change-control rule across artefacts. Each document was built on and constrained by the one before it. If a technical fact or observed behaviour contradicted a direction, the status and reasoning had to be updated, and every linked journey, behaviour rule and exception screen had to be revised in the same change.

The KISPE Space rule treated a modified visual prototype with an inconsistent specification as a documentation defect. A superseded decision received a new record rather than a silent overwrite.

This example matters because progressive specification is not only a sequence from vague to detailed. It also requires consistency across the artefact chain when understanding changes. The product was built, but Creative Navy did not support the build and has not compared the built interface against the delivered designs.

## Schone Airspace Group shows specification growing in entitlement

Schone Airspace Group shows a form of progressive specification in which the specification grew in entitlement, not only in detail. Four native integration gates were specified: terrain reference agreement; command request and observed result semantics; warning severity and lifecycle mapping; and recorded session and media identity. Each gate carried a contract, a verification sequence, the evidence that would constitute a pass and the failure disposition for what the interface must do if the source could not demonstrate the condition.

The handover protocol distinguished changes requiring UX approval from changes requiring engineering review. UX approval covered target selection, command lifecycle wording, last-known status semantics, warning acknowledgement, readiness completion, estimate revision, historical provenance and persistence of the live shell. Engineering review covered protocol event meanings, aircraft permission model, fleet size, payload commands, stream state, terrain datum, cache schema and recording keys. The specified implementation sequence was to build the shared command shell first, establish immutable aircraft and request identities, then connect per-aircraft timestamps and alert ownership.

All four gates were subsequently closed by the client's engineering functions. The claim is not that Creative Navy verified a protocol. The claim is that the design named in advance which behaviours it was not yet entitled to assert, stated what the interface must do while each condition remained open and assigned each condition to an engineering function. The product was built and is in test, not deployed.

## Raymarine shows progressive specification through observable acceptance checks and named gates

Raymarine evidence records acceptance registers across the specification set. The registers included eighteen tests on the physical control contract, twenty on detailed voice operating flows, sixteen on the calling specification, eighteen on the AIS information hierarchy, eighteen on the event priority matrix, twenty-three on the emergency specification, twenty-four verification scenarios in the exception catalogue, twenty-four on the radio and chartplotter responsibility model, ten UI acceptance criteria at handover and twenty-eight UI specification checks.

Each check was written as an observable condition testable against a prototype, a hardware mockup or a firmware implementation, not as a subjective preference. The evidence also records eight named engineering and compliance decision gates at handover, each with a dependency and a named owner: physical inputs; radio controls; the calling workflow; safety wording, timing and cancellation by market; position data; AIS freshness; chartplotter integration; and revised wording to be re-tested with occasional operators.

The Raymarine evidence should not be read as completed validation. The acceptance registers are specifications of observable conditions, not completed validations. Radio protocol behaviour, channel plans, distress procedure and final conformity remained Raymarine's responsibility. The radio was built and released, but no design-fidelity comparison is recorded.

## The handheld command-and-control engagement shows progressive specification under open ambiguity

In the handheld command-and-control engagement, the client is described as a European manufacturer of uncrewed systems, including one-way effectors, and the tactical command-and-control software that operates them. The delivery plan stated six constraints before work began: the target hardware had not been settled; requirements were shifting and that was treated as the nature of the client's situation rather than a problem to solve before design; the client preferred avoiding a large development effort but would fund one if justified; the client was not certain the multi-vehicle problem was solvable by design; design conventions including conflicts between NATO and non-NATO standards had to be observed; and the scale of the system exceeded the size of the project.

Creative Navy's documented response was the recursive ambiguity method. Creative Navy authored the requirement set first and submitted it for review and enrichment, not to settle the requirements but to establish where ambiguity sat. Each area of unknown received one of three treatments: the client sought clarification; the designs catered for a range of speculative possibilities so design could disseminate options inside the client organisation; or the area was deprioritised. The triage recurred through the project, and the fitness of the method itself was reviewed every two weeks.

The artefact carrying the work was a requirements table co-authored screen by screen, with content, actions and priority, and two facing columns for Creative Navy's comments and open questions and the client's answers. This work was led and co-authored with the client's design team, not delivered to it. The handheld interface was built; no further status is stated.

## Maritime VTS shows a chain from requirements to decisions to contracts to reconciliation

In the maritime VTS engagement, the client is described as a European vendor of maritime traffic monitoring, inland navigation and communications software for port authorities, coastal administrations and waterway operators. The evidence records twenty-eight traceable interaction requirements, each linked to session evidence, an issue cluster and a decision.

The same chain records fourteen approved decisions against eighteen explicitly rejected alternatives. Every consequential decision had a named alternative on the record and a reason the alternative lost. Reusable contracts then carried a minimum specification covering purpose and eligibility including explicit non-use cases; information model with source of truth, identifiers, timestamps, unknown values and permissions; behaviour with triggers, transitions, keyboard focus, interruption and recovery; visual portrayal including accessible text, responsive density and night mode; and quality evidence with accepted scenarios, reviewer and remaining exceptions.

Final issue reconciliation recorded 36 unique issues. Of these, 30 were mitigated in the design specifications, 4 were assigned to engineering follow-up and 2 were deferred by client decision. In this engagement, mitigated means addressed in design specifications and evaluated where in scope. It does not mean implemented in every product, proven in production, certified or cleared from formal safety review. The four safety-review candidates remained open to the client's safety authority regardless of how well they tested.

## How progressive specification differs from front-loaded specification

Progressive specification differs from front-loaded specification in timing and evidence posture. Front-loaded specification attempts to define the full system at the start from initial understanding. Progressive specification deliberately delays detail until exploration has produced enough information to justify it.

Progressive specification does not mean avoiding specification. It means specifying at the level that the current evidence can support, then increasing specificity as the work moves from research to requirements to specifications to system.

The documented examples show several forms of this movement: a controller hierarchy revised during a design block; a motion-monitoring specification revised after design reviews; an ordering platform resolved through layers and sequence; a change-control rule across artefacts; integration gates that named unresolved conditions; acceptance registers written as observable checks; a recursive ambiguity method; and a traceable path from requirements to decisions, contracts and issue reconciliation.

## Evidence boundaries for progressive specification

The evidence for progressive specification is stronger in documented engagement instances than in the standalone conceptual treatment. The term is established in Creative Navy's lexicon, but the concept is not given the same extended primary treatment as some other Creative Navy concepts.

The engagement examples do not establish measured operational results. The specifications, registers, gates and change logs describe the design work and its artefacts. They should not be read as proof of production performance, certification, regulatory conformity, deployment success or design fidelity after build unless a specific case explicitly states that status.

No single engagement should be presented as the definitive example of progressive specification. Several documented engagements provide substantial evidence in different forms, and the ranking between them is not resolved.

## Related pages

Progressive specification is most directly related to organic system building, because both concepts reject imposing a finished system structure before the system has revealed what it needs to become. It also relates to option space mapping where early exploration identifies possible directions before specification is narrowed.

The engagement examples linked from this page include AIT, The MDU, Egma, KISPE Space, Schone Airspace Group, Raymarine, the handheld command-and-control engagement and the maritime VTS engagement.
